svg.title: A nurse is admitting an older adult client who has bilateral cataracts and presbycusis. The client states, 'I don't know where anything is in here.' Which action should the nurse take first?
svg.desc: The FIRST and most fundamental fall-prevention action for a client with sensory loss is ORIENTING THE CLIENT TO THE ENVIRONMENT and ensuring the CALL LIGHT IS WITHIN REACH, which is an independent nursing action the nurse can implement immediately. A bed alarm requires a prescription, large-print discharge material is not the immediate safety need, and family presence does not replace orientation.

g.text: STUDY HUB / QUESTION MAP
Safety and Fall Prevention
Read the situation
A nurse is admitting an older adult client
who has bilateral cataracts and
presbycusis. The client states, 'I don't
know where anything is in here.' Which
action should the nurse take first?
What fits here
Orient the client to the room, including
the location of the call light, bathroom,
and furniture
Why it fits
The FIRST and most fundamental fall-
prevention action for a client with
sensory loss is ORIENTING THE CLIENT TO
THE ENVIRONMENT and ensuring the CALL
LIGHT IS WITHIN REACH, which is an
independent nursing action the nurse can
implement immediately.
